newsitem.title: USA: IBM launches 4th generation of mainframes.
newsitem.headline: IBM launches 4th generation of mainframes.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp. on Monday unveiled a much-anticipated upgrade to its microprocessor-based mainframe family with models that finally match the power of its older mainframe line.
This fourth-generation family, called the S/390 G4 Server, or G4 in short, "marks the end of the road for IBM servers using bipolar processor technology," the company said.
In 1993, IBM told its customers that by 1997, its lower-cost CMOS mainframes would be comparable in performance to its older bipolar machines.
In its first quarter, IBM's mainframe revenues fell sharply, partly because customers delayed purchases while waiting for the new, faster models.

Mainframe hardware is a key product for IBM, even though it accounts for less and less of the computer giant's total revenue. These big systems, which still run at many corporations around the world, also drive sales of IBM's mainframe software, storage and maintenance services.
IBM said its G4 server family has 14 models built on the new technology, which offers performance increases from 20 percent to 33 percent over its third-generation mainframes, IBM's G3 servers.

IBM said the G4 servers also have a cryptographic co-processor to provide customers with advanced security features for electronic commerce. IBM also said it introduced an upgrade of its OS/390 Version 2 operating system for mainframes.

The new G4 mainframe has the processing power of about 63 million instructions per second, or MIPS, which is the fastest model in this lower-cost mainframe line. The system can hold as many as 10 processors, for a total processing power of 405 MIPS.

IBM said the next version of its OS/390 is a Year 2000-ready operating system and provides enhancements to enable IBM's mainframes to be more connected to the Internet, such as the ability to run applications developed in Java, a programming language used in Internet applications.
IBM also said it enhanced its Parallel Sysplex architecture, which enables 32 separate mainframes to be linked together and to operate as one big system.
IBM's stock rose $1.625 to $87.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
